lead: GameStop / GME — is the meme stock back?
smaller: Dogecoin / DOGE — ready to run again?
Robinhood / HOOD — the app becomes a bank
Oklo / OKLO — the meltdown is an opportunity to buy
why_lead: GameStop has the strongest price and attention pairing among the crowd's names: GME closed at 28.36 USD, up 11.65% in the prior session and up 19.61% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-26), with Yahoo Finance and Reuters covering the shares' jump on 26 March (n6329, n6331).

The 26 March lead used the same bitcoin-plan catalyst for Strategy, so this repeat is kept only for what changed: a fourth-quarter beat dated 26 March (n0548) and the share reaction; the analog is re-anchored on the result rather than on the copycat sequence.
The story is simple enough for the crowd to repeat, and the bitcoin proxies moved with it (MSTR up 25.08% over 20 sessions, Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-26).
why_smaller: Dogecoin is the non-equity trade: DOGE up 16.60% over five sessions, with Stocktwits reporting retail bullish on 26 March (n1976), and a changed catalyst, the House of Doge reserve for payment adoption (n1842, n1809); the 7, 13 and 14 March runs were about the meme-coin fade, trivia prizes and the joke.

Robinhood is a changed story: the 11 March lead was the toll road, the 18 March lead prediction markets and the 25 March smaller the regulators; the banking and wealth-management launches reported on 26 March are a new product and customer event, and HOOD fell 7.10% in the prior session.

Oklo is a reversal: OKLO is down 25.06% over 20 sessions after the 11 and 13 March runs on the nuclear AI-power story; the 25 March coverage turns to whether the meltdown is a buy, with the 75-MW design and the NRC readiness assessment as new catalysts.
considered_not_chosen: Tesla as a smaller trade: eleven earlier runs, and the 26 March smaller already used the Fortune 'back in charge' and TradingView 'frenzy' items while saying the catalysts were unchanged; the Saudi launch and the Stocktwits winning streak do not change the Musk-comeback story enough to repeat it.

IonQ / quantum dip: seven earlier runs (3, 7, 12, 13, 14, 19 and 21 March); the Huang remarks are dated 20 to 22 March and the 21 March lead already used them, and the director's share purchase is a 21 March item.

Arm / ARM: the Qualcomm antitrust filing and the Stocktwits line that retail traders are skeptical (n6349) is a distinct narrative, but the feed holds only that one attention item; ARM is down 17.30% over 20 sessions in the card, so it is the reserve choice if Oklo is challenged.
Nebius / NBIS: down 31.32% over 20 sessions, but the feed has no retail-attention item on the drawdown, and CoreWeave's IPO interest has no card price.
Trump Media / DJT: an ETF-deal surge on 24 and 25 March with retail-facing headlines, but no card entry, so no price figure can be written.
Tenon Medical and SurgePays: retail-attention surges on 26 March, but no card entry.
Leveraged ETFs (TQQQ down 18.87%, SOXL down 28.53% over 20 sessions): the Thai regulatory item is a catalyst rather than attention evidence, and the theme ran on 21 March.
Reddit: down 28.49% over 20 sessions, but the only item is a 'down today' explainer, not attention evidence.
Strategy / MSTR: led on 26 March on the same bitcoin-treasury catalyst.
Rheinmetall: the largest 20-session gain in the card (39.54%), but four earlier runs (5, 10, 12 and 13 March) and institutional rather than retail attention.
Carvana: up 16.34% over five sessions with no attention item in the feed.
